title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation was invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11=29, n10=9 (guarded-only), n01=1 (baseline-only), n00=0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.2051282051 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0769230769, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory safety test for harmful over-repair (<=5% threshold) was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor; we state this omission explicitly and treat harmful-overrepair quantification as unresolved in the confirmatory claim. We report preregistration adherence, exact execution accounting, statistical inference, and limitations (synthetic faults, single model, simulator-backed success predicate), and point to archived artifacts for further exploratory auditing.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to assist network operations by producing device configurations and remediation plans. A common safety pattern is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that interposes a deterministic verifier (or simulator) between probabilistic generation and acceptance. Prior work in code, Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), and related DSLs reports that verifier-interposed repair can raise verifier-detected pass rates and provide diagnostics useful for automated repair [1], [2]. However, controlled evidence specifically targeting vendor CLIs (e.g., Cisco/Juniper) with preregistered fault operators and paired causal estimands is limited. We therefore ask: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?

Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment design and frozen task bank (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1); (2) a completed confirmatory execution under the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter using shared controlled-fault candidates and the declared model gpt-5-mini; (3) a paired analysis reporting a +20.51 percentage-point absolute increase in verifier+simulator pass rate for guarded versus baseline (p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.0769230769, 0.358974358974359]); and (4) an archived artifact bundle containing raw outputs, verifier traces, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts. We explicitly disclose that a preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis pipeline; this omission is described and its interpretational consequences are discussed.
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair architectures and verifier-interposed pipelines have been empirically demonstrated to increase verifier-detected pass rates and to supply diagnostics for model-guided repair in code and IaC settings [1], [2]. Controlled analyses also document failure modes: iterative optimization toward a single verifier can produce verifier-exploitation pathologies, and verifier mediation commonly imposes a measurable interaction / cost overhead (the "verifier tax") that affects operational feasibility [3], [4]. Surveys of LLM use in NetOps and AIOps indicate read-oriented usefulness but caution against unvalidated closed-loop autonomous changes in production networks [5]. These prior results motivate a controlled, fault-injection evaluation on vendor-CLI templates to measure post-repair residual invalidity and to audit harmful-edit incidence under paired causal semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (the paired difference in the verifier+simulator pass indicator). Design and adapter semantics: confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate was generated and shared unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and exactly one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Task bank and sampling: a deterministic fault injector produced 40 preregistered controlled-fault source candidates (manifest SHA-256 recorded). Confirmatory sample size and stopping: task_count fixed at 40; preregistered stopping required abort if the adapter contract could not be satisfied. Acceptance predicate and scoring: primary success required both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement to avoid verifier↔simulator discordance. Analysis plan: primary test was an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent); we report discordant-pair counts, absolute risk difference, and a 95% CI computed via paired-bootstrap percentile (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Missingness: the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule excludes a pair only if both condition executions fail for infrastructure reasons; one pair’s source generation was invalid/unscorable and excluded accordingly.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory test: The preregistration included a confirmatory hypothesis that verifier-guided repair would not increase harmful over-repair events beyond an absolute 5% threshold. The archived confirmatory analysis executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 produced the primary paired binary result but did not compute the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic (analysis secondary_results = []). Therefore the preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory test was not executed; we state this explicitly (no fabricated counts are reported). Exploratory audit artifacts relating to edits, validator violations, and per-episode traces are archived and available for secondary inspection but were not used to produce a preregistered confirmatory safety verdict.
sections.results:
Execution accounting: planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs); failed episodes = 2; hosted-model calls used = 118 (≤ planned maximum 120); source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Primary outcomes (complete_pairs = 39): baseline success = 30/39 (0.7692307692307693); guarded success = 38/39 (0.9743589743589743). Paired contingency table (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729).

Missingness and exclusions: one pair’s source generation was unscorable and excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule; no condition-specific infrastructure failures occurred. Sensitivity analyses and exploratory per-fault-class summaries, harmful-change audits, and contamination checks (verifier↔simulator discordance flags) are archived but were not used to alter the primary confirmatory claim. Crucially, the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor; therefore we make no confirmatory safety assertion about the preregistered <=5% harmful-overrepair threshold.
sections.discussion:
Under the preregistered controlled-challenge and shared-candidate pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the model substantially increased verifier+simulator-validated configuration success in our synthetic vendor-CLI task bank (approx. +20.51 percentage points). The shared-candidate paired design isolates the causal effect of diagnostic exposure on repair quality: both arms received the same controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets; only diagnostic exposure differed. Interpretation boundaries and implications:

1) Confirmatory scope and external validity — This confirmatory result applies to the preregistered synthetic controlled-fault bank, a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), and a single deterministic verifier+simulator. It does not establish production generality across vendors, models, or operator policies.

2) Harmful-overrepair confirmatory omission — Because the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis, we cannot confirm whether the guarded condition met the preregistered safety threshold (<=5% absolute increase). This omission reduces the paper’s ability to make a preregistered safety claim; harmful-overrepair quantification remains an unresolved confirmatory item and is listed in Limitations. Exploratory artifacts for harmful-edit auditing are archived for follow-up analysis.

3) Intervention informativeness and design — The controlled-fault injection ensured sufficient intervention activation so the diagnostic exposure could be meaningfully tested; this addresses prior concerns that interventions may be rarely activated in naturalistic data.

4) Operational considerations — The run recorded hosted-model call counts and wall-clock instrumentation (archived). The verifier tax (cost/latency) is instrumented but requires larger-scale evaluation to judge operational feasibility. Verifier-exploitation remains a potential risk for longer-horizon agentic pipelines and requires mitigation (multi-verifier ensembles, calibrated abstention, explicit uncertainty quantification).
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, controlled-fault paired experiment using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier-and-simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.0769230769, 0.358974358974359]). This effect estimate is constrained to the controlled synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived verifier/simulator. A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor; therefore we do not claim a preregistered safety verdict on harmful over-repair and report that item as unresolved. The archived artifact bundle supports independent exploratory auditing and follow-up cross-vendor, multi-model, and operational-cost studies.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Artifact availability: the execution manifest, raw_results.jsonl, provider traces, verifier traces, analysis artifacts, and hashes are archived in the evidence bundle. The run followed the preregistered stopping rule and adapter contract; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires further study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (uncertainty quantification, calibrated abstention, multi-verifier designs).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not executed: the preregistered safety hypothesis that verifier-guided repair would not increase harmful over-repair beyond an absolute 5% threshold was not computed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor; therefore no confirmatory safety verdict on that preregistered threshold is claimed here and harmful-overrepair remains an unresolved confirmatory item (exploratory audit artifacts are archived for follow-up).
